A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same echo-embeddings work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data experiments, zero-shot and fine-tuned MTEB evaluations, and robustness and error analyses, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations of compute budgets, additional model configurations and comparisons with other embedding methods.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure still repeats the input and pools representations from its second occurrence. The fine-tuning objective and basic extraction strategies remain unchanged. Describing the prompt as inducing autoencoding reframes the existing method; the new length and training-budget controls concern experimental settings.

E1.justification: v2 extends zero-shot evaluation from v1's listed 26-dataset subset to all 56 English MTEB datasets, including tasks already evaluated after fine-tuning in v1. The training collection and overall benchmark domains remain unchanged. The random-final-token corruption scenario from v1 Figure 3 is omitted.

E2.justification: v2 adds zero-shot comparisons with BERT, RoBERTa and unsupervised LLM2Vec, and evaluates bidirectional conversion without fine-tuning. It adds supervised LLM2Vec and GritLM comparisons in Table 7. Earlier leaderboard comparators remain in Appendix F. PromptEOL corresponds to v1's Jiang et al. summarization baseline rather than a newly introduced comparator.

E3.justification: The main zero-shot evaluation changes from selecting prompts using FiQA2018 to using specified fixed prompts. v2 adds S-LLaMA-1.3B configurations and experiments across inference token budgets. Its compute-matched evaluations halve echo's input length at inference and use half as many training steps. These substantially extend the evaluation design beyond v1's existing early-checkpoint training comparison.

E4.justification: v2 adds inference-budget sensitivity curves in both zero-shot and fine-tuned settings, zero-shot bidirectional-attention ablations across backbones, and further model-scale checks. Figure 2 adds results for the mixture of toy structures and last-token comparisons across both structures. The random-token robustness test and alternative-validation-set tables are omitted. Existing prompt-sensitivity, STS-error, instruction and training-progress analyses largely remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report variability across prompt choices, with the detailed appendix distributions retained. Neither introduces documented independent training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The additional prompt summary plot does not establish a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: v1 Table 1 reports echo/classical/summarization averages of 55.07/45.88/54.96; v2 Table 1 reports 48.64/42.38/43.69 under different benchmark coverage and prompt selection, so these are not same-setting declines. New results include compute-matched echo scores of 49.02 zero-shot and 64.66 fine-tuned. Original fine-tuned Mistral averages of 64.68 for echo, 63.98 for classical and 64.23 for bidirectional classical remain unchanged, as do all 56 corresponding per-dataset rows.

T1.justification: The pooling, cosine similarity, Euclidean distance and contrastive-loss definitions are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. The revised causal-attention and autoencoder discussion is conceptual explanation rather than a new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction shift from emphasizing public-data state-of-the-art performance to challenging the necessity of bidirectional architectures. New headline claims concern approaching LLM2Vec without its additional masked-language-modeling stage and remaining competitive under matched training and inference budgets. v2 also claims a clear average advantage over PromptEOL, whereas v1 reported approximately equal Mistral performance under its earlier evaluation.

C2.justification: v2 proposes preserving pretrained behavior as an explanation for advantages over bidirectional conversion and discusses Mistral's unusual benefit from that conversion without training. It develops an account of last-token failure based on the position of discriminating information and identifies small inference budgets where bidirectional classical embeddings perform better. These substantially extend the mechanism discussion and applicability boundaries beyond v1's noise sensitivity and general cost limitation.

D1.justification: v2 adds the S-LLaMA model identifier and evaluation-resource information, including approximately two days on eight A100 GPUs. Most training hyperparameters, data sources and instructions are retained. v1's explicit code and pretrained-model release link disappears; v2 states a training-data release without providing access instructions. This establishes a documentation change, not withdrawal of the resources.

R1.justification: v2 adds LLM2Vec, GritLM, DEELM, Sheared-LLaMA and repetition-for-reasoning literature. More substantially, it positions echo embeddings as an alternative to bidirectional architectural conversion and additional adaptation stages. This changes the central relationship to prior research beyond merely updating citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, synthetic-example narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Separate methodology and experimental sections become an integrated experimental narrative organized around prompts, pooling, backbones and compute. Real-data failure analyses move into Appendix E, and the appendices are reorganized. The standalone limitations section is removed, with cost discussion incorporated into the main experiments.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column layout to a predominantly single-column conference layout. Figure 2 is rebuilt into three panels; a main-text prompt summary and two compute-budget figures are added. Broad result tables are split into focused comparisons, with summarization columns and dataset counts displayed. Several zero-shot tables disappear, while retained appendix figures and tables are relocated and resized.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important unresolved practical issue: v1 acknowledged doubled inference cost, whereas v2 tests matched token budgets and identifies where repetition loses its advantage. Full-MTEB zero-shot evaluation and LLM2Vec/GritLM comparisons substantially strengthen the evidence. Removed zero-shot detail tables and the release link reduce transparency, and Figure 2's above-chance baseline bars conflict with its chance-level description. These defects temper, but do not outweigh, the stronger controlled evaluation and clearer applicability limits.
